comparison: Both evaluate experimental design and methodology (C24-C36) as supported. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of rifampicin concentration justification, MPN assay description, and exclusion criteria. Peer review affirms methods are 'robust' without specific concerns. OpenEval also covers MDK90 measurements (C37-C41, C121-C122) which peer review includes in their broader methodological affirmation.

OpenEval evaluates MDK90 quantitative measurements (C37-C41, C121-C122) as supported with appropriate statistical methods. Peer review includes these claims in their general affirmation that methods are 'robust' and results 'solid,' though without the detailed statistical assessment provided by OpenEval.

Both support the time-dependent association between isoniazid resistance and rifampicin tolerance (C44-C50). OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation using non-parametric tests. Peer review affirms this as a key finding, stating the study 'demonstrates the association of isoniazid resistant isolates by rifampicin treatment.'

Both support tolerance categorization and statistical associations (C51-C58, C123-C124). OpenEval validates the use of percentiles, odds ratios, and trend tests. Peer review affirms the finding of 'significant variation in susceptibility' with 'some cases at the same tolerance levels as bona fide resistant strains,' directly validating the key claim.

Both address growth-tolerance correlations (C62-C65). OpenEval finds claims supported but raises concern about outlier removal (C61) potentially introducing bias. Peer review affirms methods are 'robust' without questioning the outlier exclusion or correlation analyses.

Both evaluate MIC-tolerance correlations (C66-C69). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative interpretation in C68 about growth fitness mechanisms. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, affirming robustness without challenging the mechanistic interpretation that OpenEval found speculative.

Perfect claim overlap (C70-C72). Both support the finding of wide tolerance variation within mutation classes and the inference of additional determinants. Peer review explicitly notes 'no clear genetic marker for increased tolerance, suggesting multiple routes to achieving this phenotype,' directly validating OpenEval's assessment.

High claim overlap on longitudinal treatment-selection analysis (C73-C80, C125). Both strongly support the finding that rifampicin treatment selects for tolerance. Peer review explicitly affirms this 'demonstrates the association of isoniazid resistant isolates by rifampicin treatment supporting the idea that selection of MDR is a microenvironment phenomenon.'

High claim overlap on genetic microvariant analysis (C81-C87, C126). Both support findings despite limited sample size. OpenEval notes speculative nature of epistasis interpretation. Peer review affirms 'no clear genetic marker' and 'multiple routes' interpretation, and validates the microenvironment selection mechanism.

Both support main findings summary (C88-C90, C118). OpenEval validates the wide tolerance distribution and IR-tolerance association. Peer review describes this as a 'valuable study' demonstrating 'significant variation' with 'tolerance levels as bona fide resistant strains,' directly affirming the synthesis.

OpenEval evaluates assay limitations (C42-C43) as appropriately acknowledged. Peer review includes these claims in their broader methodological assessment, affirming methods are 'robust' without specifically addressing the stated limitations.

Both address growth-survival tradeoff interpretation (C91-C96). OpenEval supports the theoretical framework integration with cited literature, noting mechanistic links remain inferential. Peer review affirms methods and results without specifically addressing the theoretical interpretations.

Partial overlap on genetic-phenotypic synthesis (C97-C100). OpenEval supports microvariant selection interpretation while noting speculative elements. Peer review affirms the 'multiple routes' interpretation (C98-C99) and the microenvironment selection mechanism (C100).

Minimal overlap (C97). Both support the genetic findings synthesis. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of microvariant selection and lack of convergence. Peer review affirms the lack of clear genetic markers supporting multiple pathways to tolerance.

Minimal overlap (C100). Both support the rifampicin-driven selection conclusion. OpenEval validates this based on IR-IP longitudinal findings. Peer review explicitly affirms this supports the 'microenvironment phenomenon' interpretation.

Partial overlap on contextualization with literature (C103-C104). OpenEval supports confirmation of prior work. Peer review affirms the wide distribution finding that confirms and extends previous observations about clinical isolate tolerance variation.

Partial overlap on clinical implications (C106-C107). OpenEval supports the critique of molecular testing and stepping stone hypothesis as logical inferences. Peer review affirms clinical relevance, noting work 'will be of interest to infectious disease researchers' and supports the treatment-selection mechanism.

Partial overlap on time-dependent tolerance mechanism (C108-C110). OpenEval supports the specificity to fast-growing bacteria while noting mechanistic interpretation relies on cited literature. Peer review affirms the association and clinical implications without specifically addressing the rpoB regulatory mechanism.

Perfect claim overlap (C111-C117). Both support the stated study limitations. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of single-condition limitation and treatment regimen context. Peer review implicitly accepts these limitations by affirming methods are 'robust' without requiring additional experiments.

Minimal overlap on clinical implications (C119-C120, C127). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting recommendations are premature without clinical validation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, affirming clinical relevance and the treatment-selection mechanism, though without addressing the specific gap between research findings and clinical implementation.
